title: Pair Trade — Long MSFT / Short META (Quality Flight in Hawkish Regime)
entry: Open the pair at 1:1 dollar-notional (e.g., $25K long MSFT, $25K short META). Initiate on first day META outperforms MSFT by >1% (mean-reversion entry). Avoid entering when MSFT/META spread is at 3-month wide.
stop_loss: Pair P&L loss >5% (i.e., MSFT-META spread tightens 5% against position)
targets: META cuts capex guide while MSFT raises — +15-20% pair return
risk_reward: 1:2 — capped both ways by spread mean-reversion
catalyst: Hawkish 8-4 FOMC vote favors quality megacaps with secure cash flows over speculative-capex names. MSFT is the cleanest AI-leverage with diversified revenue (Azure, Office, Activision, Copilot). META is over-indexed on Reality Labs capex burn ($16B run-rate annual loss) and ad-revenue sensitivity to consumer spending — both vulnerable to a hawkish regime.
thesis: When the Fed signals durably hawkish (which the 8-4 April vote did), the market rewards quality cash flows and punishes speculative capex burn. MSFT and META are both 'Magnificent 7' AI names — they trade as a basket on the way up. But in a regime where rates stay high and consumer ad spending softens, the spread divergence emerges. MSFT has 4 cash-flowing AI products in market (Azure OpenAI, Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Activision gaming AI) and is a direct beneficiary of NVDA capex via Azure infrastructure rentals. META has Reality Labs (~$16B annual operating loss) and ad revenue exposure to consumer recession risk. The pair trade isolates the relative-quality bet from broad market direction — you don't have to predict whether the market goes up or down, only that quality outperforms speculative AI plays. Historical correlation 0.78, so the structural beta is low; the alpha comes from divergence on quality factors. Best entered when META has had a recent outperformance day (pair mean-reversion).
bull_case: MSFT's Azure AI revenue accelerates to 40%+ YoY in Q2; Copilot enterprise adoption hits 50M+ seats by H2 2026. META has to cut Reality Labs spending or guide ad revenue down on consumer recession signals. Spread widens 10-15% over 8 weeks. Tail: META's Q2 earnings (late July) miss on ad revenue, MSFT raises Azure guide — single-day pair P&L +5-8%.
bear_case: Reality Labs Quest/AR headset gets a viral product moment (genuine consumer breakout); META ad revenue accelerates on election-year political spending; MSFT's Azure growth disappoints on hyperscaler customer consolidation. Pair spread tightens 8-10% against position. Tail: GenAI assistant adoption shifts to META's Llama/integrated ad model, MSFT's Copilot monetization stalls.
invalidation: META Q2 ad revenue growth >25% YoY AND MSFT Azure growth <30% YoY (both confirm thesis wrong)

outcome.outcome_label: Stopped out — META outperformed MSFT by ~6.5%, exceeding the 5% pair stop
outcome.note: META surged +3.8% to $635.36 on May 27, 2026, on AI advertising tailwinds and SNOW's $6B AWS deal validating the cloud AI infrastructure thesis — while MSFT declined −0.8% to $412.65. The MSFT/META ratio moved from approximately 0.694 at entry (MSFT $419, META ~$603) to 0.650 at exit, a 6.5% tightening against the long MSFT / short META position, triggering the 5% pair P&L stop threshold. Combined pair loss: long MSFT −1.5%, short META −5.4%, totaling approximately −3.4% of total dollar-notional. META's AI advertising outperformance — AI Overviews and ad-targeting improvements — contradicted the hawkish-regime quality-rotation thesis that drove the trade at inception. final_price reflects MSFT (the reference ticker) at $412.65.
